stop_reason: The assigned CAP-009 authority gap was reduced to an implementable architecture and adversarial corpus: PayrollEngine supplies effective/knowledge-time rule selection, while ShiftGuard falsifies static compliance-label assumptions. Broader generic scheduler search stopped because RosterSpec already owns the solver/verifier plane.

candidate_dispositions.reason_detail: Runtime regulation selection combines Created knowledge cutoff and ValidFrom effective date; executable fixtures cover temporal boundaries; Timesheet validation resolves rule data at WorkTimeDate. Strong authority substrate, not a scheduler or statutory corpus.

Hard-coded BC-labeled settings lack authority/version provenance; 32h weekly rest is approximated by total hours; violating draft shifts are still persisted and test exits successfully; current official BC rules contradict some encoded semantics.
Template encodes authority-source documentation, validFrom updates, annual/mid-year change workflow and regression verification, but is not itself a current jurisdictional rule corpus.

best_result: PayrollEngine supplies the missing temporal rule-authority pattern for CAP-009: a rule version is selected by effective date plus knowledge/creation cutoff, and work-time validation can resolve date-effective constraints. Combined with RosterSpec this can produce source/version-backed schedule proof rather than static compliance settings. ShiftGuard is a concrete negative oracle showing why hard-coded numbers and warnings are insufficient.
